html:
Chersonesus was an ancient Greek colony on the southwest coast of Crimea, at today's Sevastopol, founded in the 400s BCE by settlers from Heraclea Pontica, which lasted for almost two thousand years.

Its farmers divided the land around it into regular plots for vines, still visible today. It traded grain, wine and fish across the Black Sea. It later came under Pontus, Rome and then Byzantium, as Cherson. According to the chronicle, Prince Volodymyr of Kyiv was baptised there in 988 after taking the city, before the baptism of Rus. It was destroyed in the 1300s and later abandoned. Its ruins, with a theatre and basilicas, became a World Heritage Site in 2013. Russia has controlled the site since its annexation of Crimea in 2014.
